title: Abelian tower comparison for integral ordinary systems
statement:
The Lean theorem `integralInverseSystem_abelian_comparison` has the following statement:

theorem integralInverseSystem_abelian_comparison (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (I : ∀ n : ℕ, SheafOfModules.AlgebraicInverseImage
      (Scheme.proEtaleSheafInverseImage f (Type (u + 1)))
      ((Rrings l Y).obj (Opposite.op n)) ((Rrings l X).obj (Opposite.op n)))
    (P : WeilConjectures.SemilinearSections.OrdinaryInverseSystem.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (fun n ↦ (Rrings l Y).obj (Opposite.op n))
      (fun n ↦ (Rrings l Y).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (Scheme.proEtaleSheafInverseImage f (Type (u + 1)))
      (fun n ↦ (Rrings l X).obj (Opposite.op n))
      (fun n ↦ (Rrings l X).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) I)
    (FY : Forget Y (Rrings l Y)) (FX : Forget X (Rrings l X)) :
    Nonempty (FY.F ⋙ abPull f ≅ P.pull ⋙ FX.F)

source.place: Paragraph (2): integral reduction to (Z/ell^(n+1))_n; the abelian comparison and its unit normalization are the two explicit substeps.

proof.text: For a module M and a specified algebraic inverse image I, compose the set inverse-image unit with I.moduleUnderlying.inv. This is additive: apply I.moduleAdd to the universal addition graph on the product of the underlying sheaf of M with itself, and use naturality of the set unit on the two projections and addition. Lift this additive unit to an abelian sheaf map and transpose it under the abelian inverse-image adjunction. The canonical sheafPullbackForgetIso unit equation identifies its underlying set map with the canonical comparison followed by I.moduleUnderlying.inv. It is therefore invertible, since the forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. The same formula and naturality of moduleUnderlying prove naturality in M.

For any Forget datum, use its sections equalities to build equality-transport isomorphisms from its nth forgotten sheaf to the abelian sheaf of module evaluation. Its restrictions equation gives sheaf naturality and its morphisms equation gives naturality in the module system. Its transitions equation and the unique-presheaf-restriction characterization of SemilinearSections.transition identify every horizontal arrow under these isomorphisms.

Compose the source Forget evaluation isomorphism, the abelian inverse-image comparison of step 1, the inverse component comparison of P, and the inverse target Forget evaluation isomorphism. To check horizontal compatibility, forget to sets and cancel the target component comparison and moduleUnderlying.hom. Applying underlying sets to P.transition and postcomposing with moduleUnderlying.hom changes its restriction term by P.restriction_underlying. Naturality of moduleUnderlying then yields precisely the horizontal square for the canonical set inverse-image comparison. Faithfulness gives the abelian square. Transport by the Forget isomorphisms and assemble with NatIso.ofComponents, first over tower indices and then over module systems.
